messages.author: 5c009c55dafaeed0
messages.subject: problem with yearlySiteCovs in gdistsamp
parts:
Hi All,

I'm trying to determine density of prey species at sites that were surveyed 5 times. I have a bunch of abundance covariates, and one covariate that I'd like to use for detection: julian day. I'm running the same models on different species, and for one of my species, my model runs fine, and for another I get the error "Error in optim(starts, nll, method = method, hessian = se, ...) :   initial value in 'vmmin' is not finite". I only get the error if I'm trying to use 'day' as a detection covariate.  I checked everything I could think of, and the only thing that seems to be different between the two models is that one uses the 'exponential' key function, while the error-causing model uses 'halfnormal'.  Just to see, I tried exponential with the one that gives the error, and it worked. Can anyone tell me why this might be? Is there some other formatting problem or error that I'm overlooking? Some of my code is below.

Thanks so much!

Lucretia

#read in data
dists <- read.csv("prey_distance_data_PTS_ONLY_subsample_27Nov2013.csv",header=T,sep=",")
covs <- read.csv("distance_data_covariates_BY_POINT_subsample_27Nov2013.csv",header=T,sep=",")
sites <- read.csv("yearly_site_covs_BY_POINTS_subsample_12Dec2013.csv",header=T,sep=",")

#subset for species
gsq <- subset(dists, group == "gsquirrel" | group == "gspd" | group == "")

#subset for study area, and drop levels
gs.dists <- subset(gsq, Region == "Wyoming Basin" | Region == "High Plains")
gs.covs <- subset(covs, region == "Wyoming Basin" | region == "High Plains")
gs.sites <- subset(sites, region == "Wyoming Basin" | region == "High Plains")
gs.dists <- droplevels(gs.dists)
gs.covs <- droplevels(gs.covs)
gs.sites <- droplevels(gs.sites)

#scale abundance covariates
gs.scale <- scale(gs.covs[,c(9:67)])
gs.covs2 <- data.frame(gs.scale)
gs.covs2$UID.tx.pt <- gs.covs$UID.tx.pt

#scale detection covariates
site.scale <- scale(gs.sites[,c(6:10)])
gs.sites2 <- data.frame(site.scale)
gs.sites2$UID.tx.pt <- gs.sites$UID.tx.pt

#format data
gs.Dat <- formatDistData(gs.dists, distCol="distance",
transectNameCol="UID.tx.pt", dist.breaks=seq(0,167,10),occasionCol="Occasion")

gs.umf <- unmarkedFrameGDS(y=as.matrix(gs.Dat), siteCovs=gs.covs2,numPrimary=5, 
yearlySiteCovs=list(day=gs.sites2[,c("day.1","day.2","day.3","day.4","day.5")]),
dist.breaks=seq(0,167,10), survey="point", unitsIn="m")

#models
gs <- list()
gs$minday <- gdistsamp(~sage1k+bare100+h_shrub1k,~1,~day,gs.umf,keyfun="halfnorm",
output="density",unitsOut="kmsq",mixture="NB",se=F)

parts:
Hi Lucretia,
  I can never remember what the correct order for the starting values is but I think you might need to reorder yours.  You can use "coef(MODELNAME)" to make sure you have them in the correct order.  Often, I will first run a model using the poisson mixture, as they tend to converge better, and then use those parameter estimates as starts when I try the NB mixture.  That code looks like this, with the important part in bold:

  HZ_Null_P<-gdistsamp(~1,~1,~1,keyfun="hazard", unitsOut="ha", mixture="P", output="density",data=umf)
  HZ_Null_NB<-gdistsamp(~1,~1,~1,keyfun="hazard", unitsOut="ha",mixture="NB", output="density",data=umf,
                             starts=c(as.numeric(coef(HZ_Null_P)),0))
     
Basically, it pulls the coefficients from the poisson model and then adds a starting value of 0 for the dispersion parameter.

Hope this helps!

Andrew
